input.question: how far is the nearest star as a scale model?
input.ground_truth: If the Sun was the size of a pinhead, then the nearest star would be 18 miles away. If the Sun was the size of a marble, it would be 270 miles away. If the Sun was the size of a golf ball, it would be 775 miles away. Further information: If the Sun was the size of a golf ball, the speed of light would be .02 mph, the Earth would be 15 feet away, and the Earth would be the same diameter as a mechanical pencil lead.

Question: how far is the nearest star as a scale model?

Okay! Imagine the Sun is a big grapefruit in your classroom. If we want to show how far away the next star (which is called Proxima Centauri) is, we have to go really, really far!

If the Sun is a grapefruit, then the nearest star would be like a tiny dot all the way across a football field. But even then, it’s still not far enough! In real life, the nearest star is about 4 light-years away. A light-year is how far light travels in one whole year—about 6 trillion miles!

So, if we made a scale model where 1 step = 1 mile, you would have to walk around the whole world about 7,500 times to get to the nearest star! That’s a LOT of walking! 🌟👣
